task.name: The structural-decay observer measures its readiness over every run ever recorded while analysing only a bounded window, so it refuses on a ratio its own analysis never used
task.story_text:
The structural-decay observer measures its readiness over every run ever recorded while analysing only a bounded window, so it refuses on a ratio its own analysis never used

## Observed

`python -m theforge.structural_decay_observer` reports its coverage check against the whole
recorded archive, while the window it actually analyses is bounded to the runs that carry
changed-file data. The same substrate, same data, three invocations on 2026-08-22:

```
(no --since)          92 of 734 measured cost-bearing runs join (12.5%)   THRESHOLD: NOT MET
--since 2026-08-01    92 of 194 (47.4%)                                   THRESHOLD: NOT MET
--since 2026-08-12    92 of 105 (87.6%)                                   THRESHOLD: MET
```

The numerator is 92 in all three. Only the denominator moves. Every invocation reports the same
analysed window — `2026-08-12T16:44:55 .. 2026-08-22T08:06:02` — because runs before changed-file
capture began cannot join a changed-file set at all. The default invocation therefore divides the
runs it analysed by a population most of which it did not and could not analyse, and refuses on the
result.

At the joinable-era boundary the tool reports itself, all four checks pass and the threshold is met.
Two of the other three checks were already passing at every window: 92 joinable runs against a floor
of 30, and 186 paths obtaining a comparison cohort against a floor of 1. The candidate floor —
described in `docs/plans/2348-structural-decay-observer-spike.md` as "the real gate, and it needs a
window measured in months, not days" — is also met, with 4 paths reaching 10 touching runs.

The refusal names the ratio and the required value and nothing else:

```
[FAIL] run coverage: 92 of 734 measured cost-bearing runs join to a changed-file set (need 0.8)
```

Nothing in that output indicates that the denominator is unbounded, that a bound is available, or
what bound would make the figure describe the analysed window. The recorded readiness condition for
this tool states that coverage "rises automatically as pre-#2347 runs age out of the denominator";
no aging occurs, because the default denominator has no lower bound. Measured across five further
runs the ratio moved from 10.0% to 10.6%, which reads as slow progress toward a threshold rather
than as a quantity that is not converging.

## Expected

A readiness measure is computed over the same population the tool analyses. Where a tool bounds its
own analysis — by window, by data availability, or by any other admissibility rule — the readiness
figure carries that bound too, so the number describes the evidence in hand rather than the archive
it was drawn from. Records outside the analysed population are not evidence that a readiness
condition is unmet; they are outside its scope, and including them makes the measure a statement
about history rather than about whether the tool can answer now.

A refusal also names what would resolve it. Where the shortfall is a function of how the tool was
invoked rather than of how much data exists, the output says so, because the difference between
"more runs are needed" and "this measurement was taken over the wrong population" determines whether
an operator waits or acts. A refusal that reports only a shortfall against a floor asserts that
accumulation is the remedy, and where accumulation is not the remedy that assertion is wrong in the
direction that costs the most: it converts an actionable condition into an apparent wait, and a
reader who learns that a particular refusal never means anything has learned to discount the next
one — which is the whole value of a system that declines to answer.

## Diagnosis

**Baseline:** `a8e3c9ecd2dc51de447c9f44922e600ef1227a98` captured at `2026-08-22T17:41:35.412496+00:00`

**Inspected files:**

- `src/theforge/structural_decay_observer/report.py` — `sha256:83649b7efee1bb71bc71047390196b6e9d5a87a7bc31a681dbdcd6e3e9b84e5b`
- `src/theforge/structural_decay_observer/ranking.py` — `sha256:3c09e54f427973a2b77c7851df48504c0522145076c7c13122ef0d30fb425eac`
- `src/theforge/structural_decay_observer/__main__.py` — `sha256:3f5d2c3d013f59ad2c0f9e80313a98fbe502a0939b37e49e8860a2ea78ec6484`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/audit_read_model.py` — `sha256:c0a20a3ba42fff950455984aaaf09804b9e7a23730d611127664c3b62987c42d`
- `docs/plans/2348-structural-decay-observer-spike.md` — `sha256:0c6360d534561dd05f9975623fac1cd3420d434ef2a24dd50d6910849b6b5f74`

### Observed symptom

`python -m theforge.structural_decay_observer` (no `--since`) reports "92 of 734 measured
cost-bearing runs join to a changed-file set (12.5%)" and fails the run-coverage threshold
check (needs 0.80), even though the tool's own analysed window — printed on the line right
below as "window: 2026-08-12T16:44:55 .. 2026-08-22T08:06:02" — contains only the 92 joinable
runs and none of the other 642. The 92 stays fixed across `--since` values; only the
denominator moves (734 -> 194 -> 105), and only once `--since` is set tight enough to exclude
the pre-changed-file-capture era does the ratio clear 0.80. The refusal text names only the
ratio and the required value, with no indication the denominator is unbounded by default or
that a bound is available.

### Reproduction / evidence

Read at HEAD (not re-executed against live substrate — the observed 92/734, 92/194, 92/105
figures come from the issue body, which is treated as evidence of behavior already exhibited
by the code below; the code reading independently explains why those exact numbers occur):

- `src/theforge/coordinator/audit_read_model.py:192-235` `changed_file_coverage()`: `measured`
  query counts every `audit_records` row with `total_cost_usd > 0`, filtered ONLY by the
  optional `since` parameter (clauses = ["total_cost_usd IS NOT NULL", "total_cost_usd > 0"]
  plus an optional `started_at >= ?"`). When `since` is `None` (the CLI default —
  `report.py:200` `--since` defaults to `None`), this is literally every cost-bearing run ever
  recorded, unbounded by any data-availability floor.
- Same function, lines 219-223: `joinable` (the numerator, and the source of
  `first_joinable_at`/`last_joinable_at`) is the subset with an `audit_changed_files` row —
  structurally only possible for runs recorded after changed-file capture began (referenced in
  the issue and in the spike doc as "#2347"). This population is bounded by data availability
  regardless of `since`.
- `report.py:140` prints `window: {first_joinable_at} .. {last_joinable_at}` — i.e. the
  analysed window is always the joinable era, never the full `measured` population.
- `ranking.py:400-447` `threshold_status()` computes the "run coverage" check purely from
  `coverage["run_coverage_ratio"] = joinable_runs / measured_runs` (audit_read_model.py:231)
  and renders only `"{joinable_runs} of {measured_runs} ... join to a changed-file set"` — no
  mention that `measured_runs` is an unbounded-by-default figure, nor any hint that `--since`
  changes it.
- `docs/plans/2348-structural-decay-observer-spike.md:253-254` states the design's stated
  intent for this figure: "this rises automatically as pre-#2347 runs age out of the
  denominator" — i.e. the denominator was expected to self-bound as old runs fall out of scope
  on their own, but no such aging mechanism exists in `changed_file_coverage`: `measured_runs`
  has no time decay, no changed-file-capture-start floor, and no other bound absent an
  operator-supplied `--since`.

### Hypotheses tested

- **[confirmed]** Coverage denominator (measured_runs) is unbounded by default and counts the entire historical archive, not just the analysed (joinable) window, causing the ratio to compare 92 joinable runs against a population most of which cannot structurally join.
  - Evidence: changed_file_coverage() (audit_read_model.py:192-235) computes measured_runs from every cost-bearing audit_records row, gated only by the optional `since` CLI arg which defaults to None. The joinable population (and the printed analysed window) is naturally bounded to the changed-file-capture era regardless of since. With since=None the two populations diverge maximally, which reproduces the reported 92/734 = 12.5% while the window line still reports only the joinable era.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Read the coverage/threshold/render code paths directly at HEAD; the divergence between the unbounded measured_runs query and the naturally-bounded joinable query and window printout is structural, not inferred from the issue's numbers alone.
- **[ruled out]** The observed 92/734, 92/194, 92/105 figures in the issue are themselves fabricated/incorrect rather than real tool output.
  - Evidence: The code produces exactly this shape of output by construction: since only narrows the measured_runs COUNT(*) via started_at >= ?, never touches the joinable COUNT(*) differently in a way that would change the numerator once since already excludes all pre-joinable-era runs (since 2026-08-01 and 2026-08-12 are both >= the earliest possible joinable run, so joinable_runs stays 92 in all three cases while measured_runs shrinks). This matches the issue's numbers exactly.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Derived from reading changed_file_coverage()'s SQL directly; not a re-execution against the live substrate.
- **[ruled out]** The design doc's stated self-correcting mechanism ('rises automatically as pre-#2347 runs age out of the denominator') is implemented somewhere else (e.g. a scheduled prune, a retention window) that report.py simply isn't invoking.
  - Evidence: Grepped audit_read_model.py and structural_decay_observer/*.py for any retention, prune, or capture-start-date logic; changed_file_coverage's SQL is the entire implementation of the coverage figure, and it contains no reference to a changed-file capture start date or any aging/decay logic. The 'ages out' framing in the spike doc is a plan-time assumption that was never built.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Read the full audit_read_model.py file and the observer package's report.py and ranking.py; no aging/pruning mechanism exists anywhere in this path.

### Confirmed cause

`changed_file_coverage()` in `src/theforge/coordinator/audit_read_model.py` computes its
`measured_runs` denominator (and therefore `run_coverage_ratio`) over every cost-bearing audit
record ever recorded, bounded only by the CLI's optional `--since` argument — which defaults
to `None`, i.e. no bound at all. The `joinable_runs` numerator (and the `first_joinable_at` /
`last_joinable_at` window the report prints) is structurally bounded to the era after
changed-file capture began, independent of `since`. Because the tool's actual analysis
(`build_runs`/`rank_candidates` in `ranking.py`, fed only `touch_rows` which can only exist in
the joinable era) only ever operates over that same joinable-era window, the default
invocation's coverage check divides the population it analysed by a population it did not and
structurally could not analyse. The design record's assumption that this ratio "rises
automatically as pre-#2347 runs age out of the denominator" is not implemented: there is no
aging, decay, or capture-start floor in `changed_file_coverage`, so the denominator never
shrinks on its own — only an operator manually supplying an increasingly recent `--since`
narrows it.

Support: Directly reading changed_file_coverage() (audit_read_model.py:206-235) shows the `measured`
query's WHERE clause is `total_cost_usd IS NOT NULL AND total_cost_usd > 0` plus only an
optional `started_at >= ?` when `since` is passed — no other bound. The `joinable` query adds
`EXISTS (... audit_changed_files ...)`, which is what actually restricts it to the
changed-file-capture era; this is a data-availability constraint, not a `since` filter, so it
applies identically at every `since` value including None. render() in report.py:140 prints
`first_joinable_at .. last_joinable_at` as "the window" — i.e. the human-facing statement of
what was analysed is always the joinable era. threshold_status() (ranking.py:410-418) then
reports `joinable_runs of measured_runs` as "run coverage" with no qualifier distinguishing
the two populations' different bounds. This is a direct code read, not a restatement of the
issue's own diagnosis — though the issue's prose (and the spike doc's "ages out" line) already
asserts the same underlying mechanism, so the conclusion is corroborated by, not independent
of, that framing.
Support provenance: mixed — combines direct observations with material that already stated this cause; the prior-assertion portion is not independent corroboration. The code-level mechanism (measured_runs unbounded by default vs. joinable_runs structurally bounded to the changed-file-capture era) was verified directly by reading audit_read_model.py, ranking.py, and report.py at HEAD. The issue body's own numeric trace (92/734, 92/194, 92/105) and the spike doc's 'ages out' line are prior assertions that independently point at the same cause; they were not re-executed against the live substrate in this investigation, so they corroborate rather than substitute for the code read.
Independence note: This text uses independence/corroboration language, but the cited material already stated this cause and is not independent corroboration.

### Affected code path

src/theforge/coordinator/audit_read_model.py:192-235 (changed_file_coverage — measured_runs
denominator has no bound tied to changed-file-capture availability)
src/theforge/structural_decay_observer/ranking.py:400-447 (threshold_status — "run coverage"
check and its rendered detail string report the unbounded ratio without qualification)
src/theforge/structural_decay_observer/report.py:71-118,197-212 (load_report/main — `--since`
is the only available bound and is not defaulted to the joinable/capture-era window)

### Fix-success criterion

Running `python -m theforge.structural_decay_observer` with no `--since` argument against a
substrate where changed-file capture began partway through history reports a "run coverage"
ratio computed over the same population the joinable/analysed window covers (i.e. the
denominator excludes runs from before changed-file capture was possible, or the check is
reframed so records outside the analysed population are not counted against it) — such that
the ratio, and whether the threshold is MET or NOT MET, is stable across `--since` values that
all resolve to (or fall within) the same joinable era, rather than moving from NOT MET to MET
purely as a function of how tightly `--since` happens to be set. Additionally, if the check
still fails for a genuine reason (e.g. too few joinable runs), the failure detail names what
would resolve it (more time in the current-capture era vs. a mis-scoped population) rather than
reporting only the shortfall against the floor.

### Notes

I did not re-execute the observer against the live `.forge/audits/index.sqlite` substrate to
reproduce the exact 92/734/194/105 figures — the investigation is a direct code read that
independently explains the reported behavior via the SQL in changed_file_coverage(), which is
sufficient to confirm the mechanism, but an implementer should sanity-check the live numbers
before landing a fix (e.g. confirm the earliest audit_changed_files row's started_at, to decide
whether the bound should be a fixed capture-start date, a MIN(started_at) over joinable rows,
or some other formulation). The design record (docs/plans/2348-structural-decay-observer-spike.md)
already anticipated the eventual need for a floor but assumed a no-code "aging out" that turned
out to require an explicit implementation.

handoff.summary: Bounded the structural-decay observer's readiness measure to the population it analyses. changed_file_coverage() now computes capture_start_at — MIN(started_at) over cost-bearing runs that join a changed-file set, independent of --since — and uses max(since, capture_start_at) as the lower bound for the measured_runs/measured_spend_usd denominator, so runs recorded before changed-file capture existed are outside the population rather than counted against it. The bound and what it removed are returned explicitly (coverage_floor, capture_start_at, archive_runs/archive_spend_usd, excluded_pre_capture_runs/_spend_usd) and rendered under COVERAGE, so the denominator's scope is stated rather than inferred. threshold_status() now attaches a remedy to every check: because the coverage denominator is already bounded, a shortfall there is a capture gap inside the analysed window and says waiting will not fix it, while the sample/candidate/cohort floors are labelled accumulation with the missing amount; render() prints the remedy under each failing check. When no run joins at all there is no capture era, the floor is None, the denominator stays the whole archive and the report and remedy both name that as a capture defect. Updated the spike record's reopen condition #1 (its 'ages out of the denominator' assumption was never implemented) and added a CHANGELOG entry.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
